live.instructions:
# ASO research with AppSkyline

This guide drives the AppSkyline MCP connector. Every tool below is provided by
that connector, so the user must have connected AppSkyline and be signed in to
an account with access to at least one tracked app. If a tool call fails with an
authorization error, tell the user to connect AppSkyline rather than retrying.

## Interactive workspace

Use `open_appskyline` with no arguments when the user wants to open the product
and browse visually. It is a read-only sidebar entrypoint with up to 100 items,
using the same tenant authorization as the other tools. Selection shares bounded
entity context with the host; subsequent writes still require their normal approval.

## Stores

Four stores are supported everywhere a `store` parameter appears. Use these
exact values:

`ios-app-store` · `macos-app-store` · `google-play` · `microsoft-store`

An app only has data for the stores it is registered on. When a tool returns
`store-not-configured`, the app has no id set for that store — say so and move
on rather than retrying with different parameters.

## Identifiers: two different things

Getting these confused is the most common source of empty results.

- **`appId`** is the AppSkyline app id (a uuid). Every tool that reads _your_
  data takes this: `get_app`, `list_keywords`, `get_keyword_rank`,
  `get_keyword_history`, `get_store_metadata`, `get_app_engagement_summary`,
  `list_google_play_reviews`, `add_keyword`.
- **`storeId`** is the store-native identifier: a numeric Apple id, a Google
  Play package name like `com.example.app`, or a Microsoft Store product id
  like `9wXXXXXXXX`. Only `get_store_listing` takes this, because it reads
  public listings for apps that need not be tracked in AppSkyline at all.

Start from `list_apps` when you do not yet have an `appId`. It returns each
app's id, name, default locale, and per-store ids.

## Available tools

Reading your own data:

| Tool                         | Use it when someone asks…                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_apps`                  | which apps they track; also resolves the app id the other tools need                      |
| `get_app`                    | about one app's store ids, locales and timestamps                                         |
| `list_keywords`              | which keywords they track: id, term, language, country, bid                               |
| `get_keyword_rank`           | where their app ranks right now for one term in one store and country                     |
| `get_keyword_history`        | how that rank changed over time, one row per stored search snapshot                       |
| `get_store_metadata`         | to audit their synced listing text per locale, or whether the latest version is in review |
| `get_app_engagement_summary` | how many downloads, installs, uninstalls or crashes over a period, plus top countries     |
| `list_google_play_reviews`   | what Google Play users said in the last 7 days: stars, text, version, reply state         |
| `show_app_overview`          | for a one-card overview of one app, its stores and up to 50 tracked keywords              |

Reading public or shared data:

| Tool                   | Use it when someone asks…                                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search_store_results` | which apps rank for a term right now — the competitive field                     |
| `get_keyword_overview` | how popular terms are: Google web-search volume, difficulty, CPC, up to 50 terms |
| `get_store_listing`    | about any app's public listing by store-native id — competitor research          |

Writing:

| Tool             | Use it when someone asks…                                        |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `add_keyword`    | to start tracking a term, with a country. Non-idempotent — below |
| `delete_keyword` | to stop tracking a term, by keyword id. Idempotent               |

## Batch `get_keyword_overview`; never loop it

This tool accepts up to 50 terms per call and is the one place where careless
usage costs real money. Terms missing or stale in AppSkyline's shared cache
trigger a live billable upstream lookup. Calling it once per keyword turns one
cheap request into dozens of billable ones.

Always collect the full candidate list first, then make a single call per
country. Note that `country` is required here and must be exactly two letters,
unlike most other tools where it is optional.

The volume is Google web-search demand in that country: a proxy for interest
in a term, not a count of App Store, Google Play or Microsoft Store searches.
Say so when you report it.

## Writes need the user's intent, not just their question

`add_keyword` and `delete_keyword` change the user's tracked set.

`add_keyword` is **not idempotent** — adding the same term twice creates two
rows. Before adding, call `list_keywords` and check the term is not already
tracked for that language and country. Pass a `country` with every new
keyword: the weekly rank check skips keywords that have none. When adding
several keywords, show the list and get agreement first; do not infer a batch
add from a research question.

`delete_keyword` stops future snapshots but leaves historical search data
intact, so it is recoverable in the sense that past rows survive — but the
tracking gap it creates is not backfillable. Confirm before deleting, and use
`list_keywords` to map a term the user named to its keyword id rather than
guessing.

## Reading rank results correctly

`get_keyword_rank` returns a `status` that must drive your wording:

- `ranked` — the app appears; `rank` is its position and `resultsScanned` is how
  deep the scan went. "#6 of 10 scanned" is honest; "#6" alone implies a
  ranking universe that was not measured.
- `not-ranked` — the app is genuinely absent from the scanned window. Say "not
  in the top N", not "rank unknown". Widening `num` (up to 200) can find an app
  ranked deeper.
- `app-not-found` — the `appId` is wrong. Re-check with `list_apps`.
- `store-not-configured` — the app has no id for that store.

A single rank is a point sample of a noisy series. Before calling a change a
regression or a win, pull `get_keyword_history` for the same term and country
and look at the trend. Ranks move on their own day to day. History has one row
per stored search snapshot: tracked keywords are re-checked weekly, plus any
day the term was searched in AppSkyline, so gaps between rows are normal.

## A standard ASO report

When asked for an ASO report on an app, work in this order:

1. `list_apps` → resolve the app and see which stores it is registered on.
2. `list_keywords` → the tracked set, which is the report's spine.
3. `get_keyword_rank` per important term and market, for the stores that are
   configured. Prefer the markets the user cares about over an exhaustive sweep.
4. `get_keyword_history` for terms whose current rank looks notably good or bad,
   to separate a real move from daily noise.
5. `get_keyword_overview` — **one batched call** per country over every term
   from steps 2–4 plus any candidates you are considering, to learn which terms
   are worth the effort at all.
6. `get_store_metadata` → audit titles, subtitles and the keyword field per
   locale. On Apple, check the reported character count against the
   100-character limit; unused characters there are wasted ranking surface.
7. `search_store_results` on the top few terms → who actually occupies the
   results, and `get_store_listing` on any competitor worth understanding.

Then report: where the app stands, which terms have volume the app is not
competitive on, which metadata fields are underused, and what you would change.
Rank without volume is vanity — a #1 for a term nobody searches is not a win,
and `get_keyword_overview` is what tells you the difference.

## Interactive cards

`get_keyword_rank` renders an interactive rank card, and the connector also
provides an app-overview card, in hosts that support MCP Apps. When a card
renders, do not restate its full contents in prose. Add what the card cannot
show: the trend behind the number, and what to do about it.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.title: List your AppSkyline apps
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which apps they track in AppSkyline, or an app's id is needed. Returns each app's id, name, default locale and its App Store, Mac App Store, Google Play and Microsoft Store ids, up to 100 apps. Not for finding other apps in a store.

apps.description: Apps the signed-in account can access, at most 100

truncated.description: True when the account has more than 100 apps

tools.name: get_app
tools.title: Get app details
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about one of their AppSkyline apps, such as which stores it is on or which languages it supports. Returns the app's name, default and supported locales, App Store, Mac App Store, Google Play and Microsoft Store ids, and creation and edit times. Not for the live public store page or ratings.

app.description: Null when the app is not in the signed-in account

tools.name: list_keywords
tools.title: List tracked keywords
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which keywords they track for an app, or before adding or deleting one. Returns each tracked keyword's id, search term, language, country and bid, up to 500 per call. Not for current rankings or search volume.

limit.description: Keywords to return, from 1 to 500; omit for all tracked keywords, capped at 500

skip.description: Keywords to skip before the first one returned, for paging; defaults to 0

bid.description: Bid amount stored for the keyword; null when none is set

keywords.description: Tracked keywords for the app, at most 500 per call

truncated.description: True when more than 500 keywords matched; page with skip

tools.name: search_store_results
tools.title: Search an app store
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which apps show up for a search term, or who their competitors are for a keyword, on the App Store, Mac App Store, Google Play or Microsoft Store. Returns the live results in rank order with store id, title, rating and developer (10 by default, up to 200). Not for one app's own position.

store.description: Store to search: ios-app-store, macos-app-store, google-play or microsoft-store

term.description: Search term as a user would type it in the store, 1 to 200 characters

country.description: Two-letter store country code such as US or IT; defaults to US

lang.description: Two-letter language code such as en or it; defaults to en except on Google Play, which uses the store default

num.description: Number of results to return, from 1 to 200; defaults to 10

score.description: Rating score as the store reports it

results.description: Live search results in store rank order; nothing is stored in AppSkyline

truncated.description: True when the store returned more than 200 results

tools.name: get_keyword_rank
tools.title: Check an app's keyword rank
tools.description: Use this when someone asks where their app ranks for a keyword right now in one store and country. Returns the app's live position, or not-ranked, after scanning the top 50 results by default and up to 200, and renders a rank card. Not for how a rank changed over time.

store.description: Store to check: ios-app-store, macos-app-store, google-play or microsoft-store; the app needs an id on that store

term.description: Search term to check, 1 to 200 characters

country.description: Two-letter store country code such as US or IT; defaults to US

lang.description: Two-letter language code such as en or it; defaults to en except on Google Play, which uses the store default

num.description: How many search results to scan for the app, from 1 to 200; defaults to 50

rank.description: 1-based position; null unless status is ranked

resultsScanned.description: How many results were scanned; report a rank as #N of this

tools.name: get_keyword_history
tools.title: Show keyword rank history
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how their app's ranking for a keyword has changed over time in one store and country. Returns the app's rank on each date AppSkyline stored a search snapshot, newest first, up to 365 rows; tracked keywords are re-checked weekly. Not for today's live rank.

store.description: Store to read: ios-app-store, macos-app-store, google-play or microsoft-store; the app needs an id on that store

term.description: Search term to read history for, 1 to 200 characters

country.description: Two-letter store country code such as US or IT (required)

limit.description: Snapshots to return, newest first, from 1 to 365; defaults to 365

snapshots.description: One row per stored search snapshot, newest first; rank is null when the app was not in that snapshot

tools.name: get_keyword_overview
tools.title: Look up keyword search volume
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how popular a keyword is or which keyword ideas are worth targeting. Returns monthly Google web-search volume (a demand proxy, not app-store search counts), difficulty, CPC and competition for up to 50 terms in one country. Terms missing from the 30-day cache trigger a billable lookup. Not for rankings.

terms.description: Keyword ideas to look up in one batch, 1 to 50 terms of up to 200 characters, none containing a comma

country.description: Two-letter country code such as US or IT (required)

lang.description: Two-letter language code such as en or it; optional

keywords.description: Google web-search demand per term from the shared 30-day cache, highest volume first; a proxy for interest, not app-store search counts

tools.name: get_store_listing
tools.title: Read any app's store listing
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about a competitor's or any app's public store page, such as its rating, number of ratings, price, version or last update. Returns the live listing for one store id, with description and release notes cut to 600 characters. Not for your own app's synced text per language.

store.description: Store to read: ios-app-store, macos-app-store, google-play or microsoft-store

storeId.description: The app's id in that store: numeric Apple id, Google Play package name such as com.example.app, or Microsoft Store product id

country.description: Two-letter store country code such as US or IT; defaults to the store's own default

lang.description: Two-letter language code such as en or it; defaults to the store's own default

score.description: Average rating as the store reports it

listing.description: The live public listing; description and release notes are cut to 600 characters. Null when the store has no app with that id.

tools.name: get_store_metadata
tools.title: Check your store listing and review status
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about their own app's listing text per language, such as the title, subtitle, keywords or release notes, or whether the latest version is still in review or approved. Returns the metadata AppSkyline last synced for each locale, with the version, its review state and the keyword field's length against Apple's 100-character limit; longer texts are cut to 600 characters. Not for a live competitor listing.

store.description: Store listing to read: ios-app-store, macos-app-store, google-play or microsoft-store

locale.description: Only this locale, written as in the listing such as en-US or it; every synced locale when absent

annotations.title: Check your store listing and review status

listings.description: Metadata as last synced into AppSkyline, one row per locale; it may differ from what the store shows now. Long texts are cut to 600 characters.

tools.name: get_app_engagement_summary
tools.title: Get downloads and installs
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how many downloads, installs, uninstalls or crashes their app had over a period. Returns store-reported totals, the latest 30 daily rows and top countries for one app and store; metric names differ by store. Not for keyword rankings.

store.description: Store to summarize: ios-app-store, macos-app-store, google-play or microsoft-store

startDate.description: First day of the window as YYYY-MM-DD; applies only together with endDate

endDate.description: Last day of the window as YYYY-MM-DD; applies only together with startDate

days.description: Rolling window of the last 1 to 365 days, used when no dates are given; omit dates and days for every synced day

totals.description: Store-reported totals for the window; metric names differ by store

topTerritories.description: Up to 8 leading countries or territories by downloads or installs

dailySeries.description: The most recent 30 days of one daily metric series

tools.name: list_google_play_reviews
tools.title: Read recent Google Play reviews
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what users say about their Android app on Google Play, or about recent ratings and complaints. Returns reviews with stars, text cut to 300 characters, app version, device, language and whether the developer replied, up to 100 per page. Google Play only returns reviews from the last 7 days. Not for App Store reviews.

appId.description: AppSkyline app id (uuid); the app needs a Google Play service account in AppSkyline

maxResults.description: Reviews to return per page, from 1 to 100

token.description: nextPageToken from the previous page; absent for the first page

translationLanguage.description: Translate review text into this language, such as en; omit to keep the original language

reviews.description: Reviews created or edited in the last 7 days, as the Google Play API returns them; review text is cut to 300 characters

nextPageToken.description: Pass as token to get the next page; null on the last page
